items.title: Pathophysiology, Clinical Presentation, and Treatment of Psoriasis: A Review.

items.title: Systemic pharmacological treatments for chronic plaque psoriasis: a network meta-analysis.

items.title: Systemic pharmacological treatments for chronic plaque psoriasis: a network meta-analysis.
items.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews

items.title: Drug Survival of IL-17 and IL-23 Inhibitors for Psoriasis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of drug survival for IL-17 and IL-23 inhibitors in psoriasis treatment.

items.title: Treatment of Nail Psoriasis.

items.title: Secukinumab in moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa (SUNSHINE and SUNRISE): week 16 and week 52 results of two identical, multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind phase 3 trials.

canonicalFacts.claim: Psoriasis affects approximately 125 million people worldwide and is associated with increased rates of inflammatory arthritis, cardiometabolic diseases, and mental health disorders
The IL23/IL17 axis plays a central role in psoriasis pathogenesis, validated by the effectiveness of targeted biologic treatments
Plaque psoriasis is the most common variant of psoriasis
For mild psoriasis, topical agents remain the mainstay of treatment
Nail psoriasis is associated with significant disease burden and potential progression to psoriatic arthritis

redFlags: JAK-STAT inhibitors may carry increased cardiovascular and thrombotic risks in dermatologic patients
Nail psoriasis may be more resistant to therapies than cutaneous psoriasis

excludedAgents.name: vitamin D3 supplementation
excludedAgents.reason: randomized controlled trial showed monthly vitamin D3 supplementation (100,000 IU) had no significant clinical effect on psoriasis outcomes

excludedAgents.name: secukinumab
excludedAgents.reason: failed to meet primary endpoints in two identical phase 3 trials (SUNSHINE and SUNRISE) for hidradenitis suppurativa, though this was not for psoriasis indication
